chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who performs salat (prayer) while a lamp is placed before him in the direction of the qiblah, and he said: “It is not proper for him to face fire.”
And it has been narrated that there is no harm in that, because the One for whom he performs salat (prayer) is nearer to him than that.
(890) 98. This was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr, from his father ʿAmr ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hamdānī, who raised the hadith, saying:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in a man performing salat (prayer) while fire, a lamp, and an image are before him. Indeed, the One for whom he performs salat (prayer) is nearer to him than what is before him.”
So this is an irregular narration, and along with that it is not musnad. That which proceeds in this manner is not to be preferred over many musnad reports.

key_terms.السِّرَاجُ: a lamp placed before the worshipper
key_terms.النَّارَ: fire, which is being faced during prayer
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) while a lamp or fire is in front of you?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) while a lamp or fire is directly in front of the worshipper. One narration discourages facing fire, while another permits it; the compiler concludes that the permissive report is irregular and unsupported compared to numerous connected reports. The passage is significant for prayer rulings and also illustrates hadith evaluation in Shia scholarship.
